agntux-build.tagline: Build a new AgntUX plugin for a system AgntUX doesn't yet support.
agntux-build.description:
Walks you through extending AgntUX to a new connector — search the
marketplace, install or improve, design a simple write-back UI,
preview, build, test, install, iterate against real sync output, and
submit. Built for knowledge workers, not engineers — no jargon, no
extra tools running, gratitude at every milestone, the standard
AgntUX look enforced (light mode + the shared design tokens). The
3–5-iteration sync loop is normal and expected.

supported_prompts.purpose: Walks you through building a plugin for a system AgntUX doesn't yet support. Also fixes an existing plugin if you've hit something specific (update mode).

agntux-core.tagline: The AgntUX orchestrator. Triages action items and queries your knowledge store.
agntux-core.description:
Installs first; everything else hangs off it. Maintains your `<agntux project root>/`
knowledge store, triages action items per your `user.md` preferences,
and keeps `_index.md` files in sync as ingest plugins write new data.

supported_prompts.purpose: One entry point for AgntUX. Sub-commands: onboard, profile, schema, teach {slug}, sync {slug}, ask {…}, feedback-review, triage-digest. Bare /agntux defaults to ask-mode.

ui_components.name: triage
ui_components.title: Action item triage
ui_components.purpose: The primary inline UI. Priority-sorted open action items with snooze / dismiss / done buttons and per-item suggested-action buttons that route into source plugins.

agntux-gmail.tagline: Turn your Gmail inbox into an AgntUX knowledge store, with safe drafts.
agntux-gmail.description:
Watches your Gmail inbox: emails sent to you, threads where you've replied,
and sent items awaiting follow-up. Surfaces response-needed signals,
deadlines, and decisions worth remembering. The Draft button opens an
inline composer with a pre-composed reply informed by your profile and
prior conversations with the same person. Save creates a Gmail draft and
opens it in a new tab — you review and click Send in Gmail itself. Replies
sent from Gmail auto-resolve matching items on the next sync.
data_ingested: Inbox threads where you are in to: or cc:
Threads where you have sent a message and someone has replied since
Your sent items awaiting reply for ≥3 days
Threads carrying the IMPORTANT Gmail label
Subject and snippet metadata from related threads (for reply-context)

supported_prompts.purpose: Bare or `sync` runs an ingest pass (recommended cadence: hourly). Any other first token is a live NL question about Gmail — no cursor advance, no knowledge-store write.

ui_components.name: compose
ui_components.title: Gmail reply composer
ui_components.purpose: Draft replies inline with editable to/cc/bcc/subject/body, prior-conversation context, and personalization signals. Save creates a Gmail draft and opens it in a new tab for review-and-send.

entity_subtypes.description: Email correspondents — senders, recipients, cc'd colleagues. Email address is the canonical cross-source alias used to merge with people surfaced by Slack and other sources.
Organisations resolved from sender email domains and signature blocks. Vendors, customers, partners surfaced via correspondence.
Workstreams or codenames mentioned in email subjects and bodies (often resolved via user.md → # Glossary).
Recurring themes or initiatives surfaced across multiple email threads.

action_classes.description: An email carrying an explicit due date or time-bound ask.
An email addressed to the user (to: or cc:) or a thread where someone has replied since the user's last message and a reply is expected.
An informational signal extracted from an email thread (decision summary, status update, important announcement).
Outage, incident, security, or escalation signals that warrant urgent attention.
Sales, partnership, or market signal in an email thread.
Escape hatch for items that don't fit the above; requires reason_detail.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Single JSON map (one line). Two key shapes: `inbox` for the discovery low-water-mark (Gmail epoch-seconds); `<thread_id>` for per-thread cursors (newest message internalDate processed).
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<thread_id>` for thread-rooted artefacts; `<thread_id>#<message_id>` for per-message artefacts when needed.

agntux-google-calendar.tagline: Daily look-ahead of your calendar with prep context.
agntux-google-calendar.description: Daily early-morning ingest reads the next 7 days of events across your calendars, creates action items per upcoming meeting, and enriches each with prep context — related Slack threads, Gmail conversations, prior notes — summarised inline and linked back to source. Two write-back buttons: schedule a meeting via find-a-time, and respond to an invite (accept / tentative / decline).
data_ingested: Upcoming events on all your calendars over the next 7 days
Event metadata: attendees, location, description, video conference URL, organiser
Conflicts between events on overlapping time windows

ui_components.name: schedule
ui_components.title: Find a time and schedule the meeting
ui_components.purpose: Pick attendees and a window; AgntUX surfaces free slots via Google Calendar; user picks one and Send creates the event with prep context attached.

ui_components.name: respond
ui_components.title: Accept, tentatively accept, or decline the invite
ui_components.purpose: Inline event card with conflicts and AgntUX prep links; mode tabs over a single Send button; optional note to organiser.

entity_subtypes.description: Attendees by email; cross-source merge alias candidate.
Resolved from email domains in attendee lists.
Codename mined from event titles and descriptions; resolved via user glossary.
Recurring meeting themes — standups, weekly syncs, customer reviews.

action_classes.description: An event with hard prep work due before start; e.g. review deck, submit Q3 numbers.
An invite the user has not yet responded to.
An upcoming meeting the user is attending needs prep context surfaced before start.
A recurring meeting whose summary or outcome should be captured post-event.
Escape hatch for calendar events not fitting the above classes.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: JSON map with `look_ahead_window_end` (RFC3339) and per-event `<calendar_id>#<event_id>` → `updated` timestamp pairs. Past events evict on each sync pass.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<calendar_id>#<event_id>` for events; add `#<occurrence_start>` for recurring event instances.

agntux-slack.tagline: Turn your Slack workspace into an AgntUX knowledge store, with safe drafts.
agntux-slack.description:
Watches your Slack DMs, @mentions, and active threads; extracts people,
companies, projects, and topics. Surfaces response-needed signals,
deadlines, and decisions. One-click buttons — Draft, Schedule, Open in
Slack, Mark done — open the reply iframe with a pre-composed draft
informed by your profile and prior action items. Replies sent in Slack
auto-resolve matching open items on the next sync. The iframe Send
button is the explicit authorisation gate for any Slack write.
data_ingested: DMs (1:1) and group DMs in your workspace
@mentions of you in any channel you have access to
Threads where you are OP or have replied
Channel messages in any channel you have authored in recently
Pinned messages and canvases referenced from monitored channels

supported_prompts.purpose: Bare or `sync` runs an ingest pass (recommended cadence: every 30 min, 7am–7pm weekdays local). Any other first token is a live NL question about Slack — no cursor advance, no knowledge-store write.

ui_components.name: compose
ui_components.title: Slack reply composer
ui_components.purpose: Draft replies inline with thread context, editable body, and mode tabs (Send / Schedule / Save draft). Personalization signals visible. Send button commits the action.

ui_components.name: canvas
ui_components.title: Slack canvas summariser
ui_components.purpose: Summarize threads to Slack canvases inline. Edit title, TL;DR, decisions, open questions, and participants. Create button posts the canvas to the thread.

entity_subtypes.description: Slack users — DM partners, channel co-authors, mentioned colleagues. Email from profile is the cross-source alias.
Organizations referenced in Slack — vendors, customers, partners surfaced via shared links or named in messages.
Workstreams or codenames mentioned in channels and threads (often resolved via user.md → # Glossary).
Recurring themes, products, or initiatives surfaced across multiple Slack threads.

action_classes.description: A Slack message carrying an explicit due date or time-bound ask.
A DM, @mention, vote/poll, or thread reply that expects a response from the user.
An informational signal extracted from a Slack thread (decision, status update, pinned message).
Outage/incident/security signal in a monitored ops or security channel; @here / @channel pings to high-stakes channels.
Competitor or market signal in a sales/marketing channel; prospect activity or partnership cues.
Escape hatch for items that don't fit the above; requires reason_detail.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Single JSON map (one line) under `cursor`. Two key shapes: `<channel_id>` for channel cursors (newest parent ts), `<channel_id>#<thread_ts>` for thread cursors (newest reply ts).
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<channel_id>#<thread_ts>` for thread-rooted artefacts; `<channel_id>#<ts>` for non-threaded messages.
